defs.def:causal-query: For \(a\in\mathcal X_A\), set \(Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)=P_{\mathcal M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))\), and set \(\tau_{s_Y}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)\{Q_{a_1}^{\mathcal M}(y)-Q_{a_0}^{\mathcal M}(y)\}\).
defs.def:observational-fiber: \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G):P_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}}\}\).
defs.def:positive-rm-class: \(\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G):|\mathcal X_Z|<\infty\text{ for every }Z\in\mathcal V\cup\mathcal R\cup\mathcal V^{\dagger},\ \mathcal G\text{ is regular and maximal},\ P_{\mathcal M}(v,r)>0\text{ for every }(v,r)\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\}\).
defs.def:published-lm-class: \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G)\) is the published ambient class of semi-Markovian labeled-missingness SCMs on the finite vertex graph \(\mathcal G\): endogenous and exogenous state spaces may be measurable categorical or continuous standard Borel spaces, structural maps are measurable, the individual bidirected-edge and private exogenous factors are mutually independent, the proxy equations satisfy proxy consistency, and every labeled mechanism deletion has the semantics encoded by \(\mathcal G\). defs.def:response-polynomial-fiber:
Let
\[
L_{\mathcal G}=\left|\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\right|,
\qquad
K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)=L_{\mathcal G}+|\mathcal X_A|(|\mathcal X_Y|-1),
\qquad
\mathcal J=\mathcal E^{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal G)\sqcup\mathcal V\sqcup\mathcal R.
\]
The integer \(K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\) is a universal factorwise upper bound, not a claimed sharp support size. For \(g\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}\) introduce \(\gamma_g\), and for \(h\in\mathcal J\) and \(1\leq k\leq K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\) introduce \(\rho_{h,k}\). For a full cell \((v,r)\), define
\[
p_{v,r}(\theta)=
\sum_{g\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}}
\sum_{u\in\{1,\ldots,K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\}^{\mathcal J}}
\mathbf 1\{g(u)=(v,r)\}\gamma_g\prod_{h\in\mathcal J}\rho_{h,u_h},
\qquad
p_o(\theta)=\sum_{(v,r):\operatorname{proxy}(v,r)=o}p_{v,r}(\theta).
\]
Define \(q_{a,y}(\theta)\) by the same product sum after replacing the selected equation for \(A\) by the constant \(a\). With formal observed coordinates \(\mathbf p=(p_o)_o\), set
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p):={}&
\bigwedge_{g\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}}(\gamma_g^2-\gamma_g=0)
\ \wedge\ \sum_g\gamma_g=1\\
&\wedge\bigwedge_{h\in\mathcal J}
\left(\bigwedge_{k=1}^{K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)}\rho_{h,k}\geq0
\ \wedge\ \sum_{k=1}^{K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)}\rho_{h,k}=1\right)\\
&\wedge\bigwedge_{(v,r)}p_{v,r}(\theta)>0
\ \wedge\ \bigwedge_{o\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}}p_o(\theta)=p_o.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus every individual bidirected-edge or private factor has its own simplex and the joint latent law is the product over \(h\). The one-hot equations select one graph-wide tuple of label-compatible deterministic tables; they do not mix structural tables through an additional unrestricted district latent.

assumptions.ass:finite-alphabets: \(|\mathcal X_Z|<\infty\) for every \(Z\in\mathcal V\cup\mathcal R\cup\mathcal V^{\dagger}\).
assumptions.ass:label-semantics: Every label \((X,Z,R_X=0)\) in \(\mathcal G\) encodes that the structural mechanism for \(Z\) omits \(X\) in context \(R_X=0\).
assumptions.ass:proxy-consistency: For every partially observed \(Z\in\mathcal V\), \(Z^{\dagger}=Z\) when \(R_Z=1\) and \(Z^{\dagger}=\star\) when \(R_Z=0\).
assumptions.ass:semimarkovian: \(\mathcal M\) has one exogenous factor shared by the two endpoints of each bidirected edge of \(\mathcal G\), one private exogenous factor for each substantive or missingness vertex, and all these factors are mutually independent.
assumptions.ass:strict-positivity: \(P_{\mathcal M}(v,r)>0\) for every \((v,r)\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\).
assumptions.ass:acyclic: The directed part of \(\mathcal G\) is acyclic.
assumptions.ass:regular: The label set of \(\mathcal G\) is regular.
assumptions.ass:maximal: The label set of \(\mathcal G\) is maximal.

thm:tcf-soundness.proof_tex:
Fix an identifying cell \(\psi_j\), put
\[
\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}}=(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o):o\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}),
\]
and suppose that \(\psi_j(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})\) holds.  Fix
\(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  By
\(\mathrm{def{:}observational\text{-}fiber}\), this model is in
\(\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\) and induces
\(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).  The forward implication of
\(\mathrm{thm{:}response\text{-}fiber\text{-}equivalence}\) therefore supplies a response vector
\(\theta_{\mathcal M}\) satisfying
\[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta_{\mathcal M};\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})
\quad\text{and}\quad
q_{a,y}(\theta_{\mathcal M})=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
\quad
\text{for every }(a,y)\in\mathcal X_A\times\mathcal X_Y.
\tag{1}
\]
In particular, the feasible response fiber over \(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is nonempty.  The strict inequalities in
\(\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}\) also state that every full-data cell polynomial is positive, as required by
\(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}positivity}\).

Fix \((a,y)\in\mathcal X_A\times\mathcal X_Y\).  Because \(\psi_j\) is identifying for this coordinate,
\(\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})\) is true.  Expanding
\(\mathrm{def{:}terminal\text{-}qe\text{-}test}\), this means
\[
\neg\exists\theta^0\,\exists\theta^1
\left[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^0;\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})
\wedge
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^1;\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})
\wedge
q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\ne q_{a,y}(\theta^1)
\right].
\tag{2}
\]
Thus any two feasible response vectors have the same \(q_{a,y}\)-value.  By (1), at least one feasible vector exists.  Hence the relation
\[
\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}},z)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists\theta\left[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})
\wedge z=q_{a,y}(\theta)
\right]
\tag{3}
\]
has exactly one real solution, denoted \(z_{a,y}\).  Substituting \(\theta_{\mathcal M}\) from (1) into (3) gives
\[
z_{a,y}=q_{a,y}(\theta_{\mathcal M})=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).
\tag{4}
\]

It remains to check that either allowed representation of the cell functional evaluates to this unique value.  If the cell stores the graph relation (3), then
\(\mathrm{def{:}symbolic\text{-}observed\text{-}partition}\) and the definition of the successful output give
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=z_{a,y}.
\tag{5}
\]
Otherwise, \(\mathrm{def{:}tcf\text{-}procedure}\) stores a rational trace
\(r(\mathbf p)=N(\mathbf p)/D(\mathbf p)\) only after verifying on the whole cell that
\[
\forall\mathbf p\,\forall z\,
\left[
\psi_j(\mathbf p)\wedge\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p,z)
\Longrightarrow
D(\mathbf p)\ne0\wedge D(\mathbf p)z=N(\mathbf p)
\right].
\tag{6}
\]
Apply (6) to \(\mathbf p=\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(z=z_{a,y}\).  The premises hold by the choice of the cell and (3), so
\[
D(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})\ne0,
\qquad
D(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})z_{a,y}=N(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{7}
\]
The first relation in (7) licenses division; the second then yields
\[
r(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})=z_{a,y}.
\tag{8}
\]
The annotated-cell definition of \(f_{a,j}\), together with (5) in the graph-relation case and (8) in the rational case, proves
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)
=z_{a,y}
=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).
\tag{9}
\]
The choices of \(\mathcal M\), \(a\), and \(y\) were arbitrary, so (9) proves the coordinatewise assertion throughout the entire compatible positive fiber, rather than merely at a response-vector oracle.

We record explicitly the direct score-contrast bridge used by the target-only refinement.  For a feasible response vector define the proof intermediate
\[
t_{s_Y}(\theta)
=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)
\left\{q_{a_1,y}(\theta)-q_{a_0,y}(\theta)\right\}.
\tag{10}
\]
The sum is finite because membership in \(\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\), as specified by \(\mathrm{def{:}positive\text{-}rm\text{-}class}\), makes \(\mathcal X_Y\) finite.  Applying (1) at \(a_1\) and \(a_0\), and then using \(\mathrm{def{:}causal\text{-}query}\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
t_{s_Y}(\theta_{\mathcal M})
&=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)
\left\{Q_{a_1}^{\mathcal M}(y)-Q_{a_0}^{\mathcal M}(y)\right\}\\
&=\tau_{s_Y}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
Consequently, if a cell satisfies the direct constancy formula
\[
\neg\exists\theta^0\,\exists\theta^1
\left[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^0;\mathbf p)
\wedge
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^1;\mathbf p)
\wedge
t_{s_Y}(\theta^0)\ne t_{s_Y}(\theta^1)
\right],
\tag{12}
\]
then at \(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}}\) its unique-value relation
\[
\exists\theta\left[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})
\wedge z=t_{s_Y}(\theta)
\right]
\tag{13}
\]
has the unique solution \(z=\tau_{s_Y}\), by (1), (11), and (12).  The same argument as (6)--(8) shows that any rational annotation certified by the corresponding whole-cell implication also equals \(\tau_{s_Y}\).  This argument treats the finitely many values \(s_Y(y)\) as supplied real coefficients; it neither assumes that they are rational nor requires a finite encoding of them for the mathematical equality.

Finally, the displayed consequence in the theorem follows directly from (9): finiteness permits termwise substitution, so
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)
\left\{f_{a_1,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)-f_{a_0,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\right\}\\
&\qquad=
\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)
\left\{Q_{a_1}^{\mathcal M}(y)-Q_{a_0}^{\mathcal M}(y)\right\}
=\tau_{s_Y},
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
where the last equality is \(\mathrm{def{:}causal\text{-}query}\).  All divisions used above are justified by the nonzero-denominator implication (6), and all conditioning and support needed to construct the response fiber is contained in the positive-fiber equivalence (1).  This completes the proof.

snapshot.stmt: For every identifying cell \(\psi_j(\mathbf p)\in\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\), every compatible law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfying \(\psi_j((P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o))_o)\), every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), every \(a\in\mathcal X_A\), and every \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), the cell's functional satisfies \[f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).\] Consequently, \(\sum_y s_Y(y)\{f_{a_1,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)-f_{a_0,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\}=\tau_{s_Y}\) throughout that fiber. This is a mathematical specialization statement and does not require a finite encoding of the population coordinates.

defs.def:causal-query: For \(a\in\mathcal X_A\), set \(Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)=P_{\mathcal M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))\), and set \(\tau_{s_Y}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)\{Q_{a_1}^{\mathcal M}(y)-Q_{a_0}^{\mathcal M}(y)\}\).
defs.def:colored-fixing: If \(v\) is fixable in \(\mathcal H\) and license \(\lambda\) is valid on the trace recorded by \(\kappa\), \(\Phi_v^{\lambda}\) moves \(v\) from the random to the fixed set, deletes arrowheads into \(v\), replaces \(q\) by \(q/q(v\mid\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal H}(v))\), applies the same division to \(\pi\), and appends \(\lambda\) and its current provenance to \(\Lambda\).
defs.def:context-selection: For a missingness assignment \(c'\) compatible with the current trace, \(\Sigma_{c'}(\kappa)\) restricts \(q\) and \(\pi\) to \(c'\), normalizes on the positive selected cell, deletes the edges carrying labels activated by \(c'\), and retains every earlier entry of \(\Lambda\).
defs.def:observational-fiber: \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G):P_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}}\}\).
defs.def:positive-rm-class: \(\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G):|\mathcal X_Z|<\infty\text{ for every }Z\in\mathcal V\cup\mathcal R\cup\mathcal V^{\dagger},\ \mathcal G\text{ is regular and maximal},\ P_{\mathcal M}(v,r)>0\text{ for every }(v,r)\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\}\).
defs.def:response-polynomial-fiber:
Let
\[
L_{\mathcal G}=\left|\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\right|,
\qquad
K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)=L_{\mathcal G}+|\mathcal X_A|(|\mathcal X_Y|-1),
\qquad
\mathcal J=\mathcal E^{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal G)\sqcup\mathcal V\sqcup\mathcal R.
\]
The integer \(K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\) is a universal factorwise upper bound, not a claimed sharp support size. For \(g\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}\) introduce \(\gamma_g\), and for \(h\in\mathcal J\) and \(1\leq k\leq K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\) introduce \(\rho_{h,k}\). For a full cell \((v,r)\), define
\[
p_{v,r}(\theta)=
\sum_{g\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}}
\sum_{u\in\{1,\ldots,K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\}^{\mathcal J}}
\mathbf 1\{g(u)=(v,r)\}\gamma_g\prod_{h\in\mathcal J}\rho_{h,u_h},
\qquad
p_o(\theta)=\sum_{(v,r):\operatorname{proxy}(v,r)=o}p_{v,r}(\theta).
\]
Define \(q_{a,y}(\theta)\) by the same product sum after replacing the selected equation for \(A\) by the constant \(a\). With formal observed coordinates \(\mathbf p=(p_o)_o\), set
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p):={}&
\bigwedge_{g\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}}(\gamma_g^2-\gamma_g=0)
\ \wedge\ \sum_g\gamma_g=1\\
&\wedge\bigwedge_{h\in\mathcal J}
\left(\bigwedge_{k=1}^{K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)}\rho_{h,k}\geq0
\ \wedge\ \sum_{k=1}^{K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)}\rho_{h,k}=1\right)\\
&\wedge\bigwedge_{(v,r)}p_{v,r}(\theta)>0
\ \wedge\ \bigwedge_{o\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}}p_o(\theta)=p_o.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus every individual bidirected-edge or private factor has its own simplex and the joint latent law is the product over \(h\). The one-hot equations select one graph-wide tuple of label-compatible deterministic tables; they do not mix structural tables through an additional unrestricted district latent.
defs.def:symbolic-observed-partition:
Conjoin the simplex formula \(p_o\geq0\), \(\sum_op_o=1\), and the feasible-projection formula \(\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\) with every quantifier-free output of \(\mathsf I_{a,y}\), refine their common sign-invariant CAD, and discard infeasible cells. The remaining pairwise-disjoint formulas \(\psi_1(\mathbf p),\ldots,\psi_J(\mathbf p)\) form the coordinate partition \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\). Each coordinate cell stores, for every \((a,y)\), either \(\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p,z)\) or \(\mathsf W_j(\mathbf p,a,y,\theta^0,\theta^1)\).

Independently introduce the formal score coordinates \(\mathbf s=(s_y:y\in\mathcal X_Y)\). Conjoin the lifted coordinate-cell formulas with the quantifier-free output of \(\mathsf I_{\tau}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\), refine by one common sign-invariant CAD in \((\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\), and discard points whose \(\mathbf p\)-coordinate is infeasible. The resulting pairwise-disjoint formulas \(\chi_1(\mathbf p,\mathbf s),\ldots,\chi_K(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\) form
\[
\mathscr P^{\tau}_{\mathcal G,A,Y}
\quad\text{on}\quad
\{\mathbf p:\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\}
\times\mathbb R^{\mathcal X_Y}.
\]
This target partition refines the lift of the coordinate partition. Each target cell stores either the unique-value relation \(\mathsf V_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s,z)\) or the witness relation \(\mathsf W_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s,\theta^0,\theta^1)\). Thus coordinate negativity and target negativity are recorded separately.
defs.def:tcf-procedure:
On formal input \((\mathcal G,A,Y,\mathbf p)\), first construct the response-polynomial feasibility formula \(\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\), all coordinate-constancy formulas \(\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p)\), and the direct target-constancy formula \(\mathsf I_{\tau}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\) with \(\mathbf s\) retained as a formal real vector. Run one signed-subresultant CAD for the coordinate family in \(\mathbf p\), and a second signed-subresultant CAD for the target family in \((\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\) together with the lifted coordinate-cell polynomials. This produces the canonical coordinate cells \(\psi_j\) and target cells \(\chi_k\), with their respective unique-value or witness relations, before any fixing trace is enumerated.

After both base partitions have been fixed, enumerate expression-discovery traces. Start from every supported observed margin and partial-context trace kernel written as a rational expression in \(\mathbf p\). Recursively branch only by strict ancestral marginalization, restriction to a proper child of a nontrivial district decomposition, a licensed \(\Phi_v^{\lambda}\) update, or a delayed \(\Sigma_{c'}\) update that strictly extends the partial context. Retain the complete operation word and memoize only literal complete tuples \(\kappa=(\mathcal H,F,c,q,\pi,\Lambda)\), including the syntax of \(q\), \(\pi\), and every provenance entry in \(\Lambda\). An adjacent-swap optimization may merge branches only after replaying both license orders from their common pre-swap state in a fixed canonical order and verifying literal equality of the complete resulting tuples. Fixing and selection are never commuted.

For a candidate coordinate expression \(r(\mathbf p)=N(\mathbf p)/D(\mathbf p)\), a coordinate cell \(\psi_j\), and \((a,y)\) having a unique relation, decide
\[
\forall\mathbf p\,\forall z
\left[
\psi_j(\mathbf p)\wedge\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p,z)
\Longrightarrow
D(\mathbf p)\neq0\wedge D(\mathbf p)z=N(\mathbf p)
\right].
\]
For a candidate direct-target expression \(r_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)=N_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)/D_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\), formed as a score-linear combination of compatible trace expressions, and a target cell \(\chi_k\) having a unique relation, decide
\[
\forall\mathbf p\,\forall\mathbf s\,\forall z
\left[
\chi_k(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\wedge\mathsf V_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s,z)
\Longrightarrow
D_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\neq0
\wedge D_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)z=N_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)
\right].
\]
Annotate a cell only when its implication is true. If no candidate passes, retain the corresponding unique-value graph; on a nonconstant coordinate or target cell retain \(\mathsf W_j\) or \(\mathsf W_{\tau}\), respectively. Trace enumeration and annotation never split, merge, or otherwise alter either base partition. The notation \(\operatorname{TCF}(\mathcal G,A,Y,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) denotes the two symbolic partitions and their verified annotations, with formal names \(p_o=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o)\); a supplied \(s_Y\) selects the target-score section only at mathematical or exact specialization. The procedure neither names nor returns a colored hedge.
defs.def:terminal-qe-test:
For every \(a\in\mathcal X_A\) and \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), use disjoint copies \(\theta^0=(\gamma^0,\rho^0)\) and \(\theta^1=(\gamma^1,\rho^1)\) and eliminate precisely those response variables from
\[
\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p):=
\neg\exists\theta^0\,\exists\theta^1
\left[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^0;\mathbf p)
\wedge\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^1;\mathbf p)
\wedge q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1)
\right].
\]
The only free variables in this coordinate formula are the \(|\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}|\) coordinates \(\mathbf p\). On its true region define
\[
\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p,z):=
\exists\theta
\left[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)
\wedge z=q_{a,y}(\theta)
\right],
\]
and on its false region use the unnegated doubled conjunction \(\mathsf W_j(\mathbf p,a,y,\theta^0,\theta^1)\).

For a formal real score vector \(\mathbf s=(s_y:y\in\mathcal X_Y)\), define the target polynomial
\[
t_{\mathbf s}(\theta)
=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_y
\{q_{a_1,y}(\theta)-q_{a_0,y}(\theta)\}
\]
and the direct target-constancy formula
\[
\mathsf I_{\tau}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p,\mathbf s):=
\neg\exists\theta^0\,\exists\theta^1
\left[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^0;\mathbf p)
\wedge\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^1;\mathbf p)
\wedge t_{\mathbf s}(\theta^0)\neq t_{\mathbf s}(\theta^1)
\right].
\]
Its only free variables are \((\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\). On its true region define
\[
\mathsf V_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s,z):=
\exists\theta
\left[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)
\wedge z=t_{\mathbf s}(\theta)
\right],
\]
and on its false region define
\[
\mathsf W_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s,\theta^0,\theta^1):=
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^0;\mathbf p)
\wedge\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^1;\mathbf p)
\wedge t_{\mathbf s}(\theta^0)\neq t_{\mathbf s}(\theta^1).
\]
Quantifier elimination returns quantifier-free polynomial-sign formulas in the displayed free variables. No rationality or algebraicity is imposed on a supplied score map for the mathematical constancy assertion; represented point extraction is deferred to exact specialization.

thm:tcf-termination.proof_tex:
For a trace state \(\kappa\), let \(r(\kappa)\) be the number of random vertices in its CADMG and let \(d(c)\) be the number of missingness indicators assigned by its partial context. Define
\[
\mu(\kappa)=r(\kappa)+|\mathcal R|-d(c).
\tag{1}
\]
This is a nonnegative integer initially at most \(2n\). Under \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\), strict ancestral marginalization, restriction to a proper district child, and fixing each reduce the random set, while delayed selection strictly increases \(d(c)\). Hence every operation word has length at most \(2n\).

There are at most \(2^n\) observed margins and
\[
c=\prod_{R_Z\in\mathcal R}(|\mathcal X_{R_Z}|+1)
\tag{2}
\]
partial contexts. The two subset operations contribute at most \(2^{n+1}\) choices, fixing contributes at most \(n(\ell+1)\), selection contributes at most \(c\), and one terminal marker contributes one. Thus
\[
L_{\mathrm{op}}=2^{n+1}+n(\ell+1)+c+1,
\qquad
B_{\mathrm{state}}=2^n c\sum_{j=0}^{2n}L_{\mathrm{op}}^j.
\tag{3}
\]
For a fixed initial trace and operation word, every component of \(\kappa=(\mathcal H,F,c,q,\pi,\Lambda)\) is prescribed. Therefore (3) bounds the literal complete states, including every operation order and provenance list. By \(\text{lem:colored-adjacent-swap}\), kernel commutation alone does not erase unequal trace suffixes; the optional canonical-replay merge in \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\) only decreases (3).

Write \(h=|\mathcal E^{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal G)|+|\mathcal V|+|\mathcal R|\) and \(g=|\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}|\). A doubled coordinate or target formula uses at most \(2\{g+hK_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\}\) response coordinates and \(|\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}|\) free observed coordinates; the target formula additionally has \(|\mathcal X_Y|\) free score coordinates. Hence their variable counts are bounded by
\[
p_{\mathrm{coord}}=2\{g+hK_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\}+|\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}|,
\qquad
p_{\tau}=2\{g+hK_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\}+|\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}|+|\mathcal X_Y|.
\tag{4}
\]
Their complete encodings have length at most \(s\) by \(\text{def:termination-budget}\). The definition of \(\operatorname{CAD}(m,b)\) therefore bounds the two trace-independent base calls by
\[
C_{\mathrm{coord}}=\operatorname{CAD}(p_{\mathrm{coord}},s),
\quad
C_{\tau}=\operatorname{CAD}(p_{\tau},s),
\quad
C_{\mathrm{base}}=C_{\mathrm{coord}}+C_{\tau}.
\tag{5}
\]

Each visited trace offers at most one candidate for each coordinate and coordinate cell, and at most one direct-target candidate for each target cell. Consequently the number of whole-cell tests is at most
\[
N_{\mathrm{check}}
=B_{\mathrm{state}}
\left\{|\mathcal X_A||\mathcal X_Y|C_{\mathrm{coord}}+C_{\tau}\right\}.
\tag{6}
\]
After denominators are cleared, a coordinate test contains at most one response vector, \(z\), and \(\mathbf p\); a target test contains at most one response vector, \(z\), \(\mathbf p\), and \(\mathbf s\). Thus each has at most \(p_{\max}+1\) variables and encoding length at most \(s\). Each is decided within \(\operatorname{CAD}(p_{\max}+1,s)\) steps. Summing (3), (5), and (6) proves
\[
B_{\mathrm{tot}}
=B_{\mathrm{state}}+C_{\mathrm{base}}
+N_{\mathrm{check}}\operatorname{CAD}(p_{\max}+1,s).
\tag{7}
\]

Both partitions contain finitely many integer-polynomial signs. The exact observed-law interface decides the coordinate signs, and the augmented exact interface decides the joint observed-law and score signs. Standard finite root isolation from the fixed CAD implementation then supplies the asserted Thom encodings over the corresponding generated ordered field. These specialization steps are finite and separate from (7). No step defines computation on an unencoded real or gives a polynomial bound.

Let the quantities in \(\text{def:termination-budget}\) be fixed. For every finite \(\mathcal G\) and finite alphabets, the expression-discovery phase of \(\operatorname{TCF}(\mathcal G,A,Y,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) visits at most
\[
B_{\mathrm{state}}=2^n c\sum_{j=0}^{2n}
\bigl\{2^{n+1}+n(\ell+1)+c+1\bigr\}^j
\]
literal complete trace states \(\kappa=(\mathcal H,F,c,q,\pi,\Lambda)\), counting every fixing-selection interleaving and provenance-bearing history. Independently of those traces, the coordinate and direct-target base CADs construct \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\) and \(\mathscr P^{\tau}_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\) within
\[
C_{\mathrm{base}}
=\operatorname{CAD}(p_{\mathrm{coord}},s)
+\operatorname{CAD}(p_{\tau},s)
\]
projection, root-isolation, sign-evaluation steps, and output cells. At most
\[
N_{\mathrm{check}}
=B_{\mathrm{state}}
\left\{|\mathcal X_A||\mathcal X_Y|
\operatorname{CAD}(p_{\mathrm{coord}},s)
+\operatorname{CAD}(p_{\tau},s)\right\}
\]
coordinate and target whole-cell candidate-equality sentences are subsequently decided, and the total work is bounded by
\[
B_{\mathrm{tot}}
=B_{\mathrm{state}}+C_{\mathrm{base}}
+N_{\mathrm{check}}\operatorname{CAD}(p_{\max}+1,s).
\]
Given \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), coordinate-cell selection and represented value or witness extraction terminate after finitely many exact sign decisions. Given \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},s_Y)\), the same is true for the direct-target cell over the ordered field generated by the observed and score coordinates. defs.def:exact-observed-specialization:
Given \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), decide the finitely many integer-polynomial signs in \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\) using rational arithmetic, algebraic-number arithmetic with the supplied square-free polynomials and isolating intervals, or the supplied exact-real sign oracle, and choose the unique coordinate cell containing \(p_o=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o)\). On an identifying coordinate cell, represent its unique value; on a negative coordinate cell, choose \(\theta^0,\theta^1\) satisfying \(\mathsf W_j\), by Thom encodings over the real closure of the ordered field generated by \(\mathbf p\).

For the direct target partition, \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},s_Y)\) additionally supplies each score coordinate \(s_Y(y)\) as a rational number, a real-algebraic number with square-free polynomial and isolating interval, or through an exact-real oracle deciding the sign of every integer polynomial at the concatenated vector \((\mathbf p,\mathbf s_Y)\). Decide the finitely many signs in \(\mathscr P^{\tau}_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\) and choose its unique cell containing \((\mathbf p,\mathbf s_Y)\). On a target-identifying cell, represent the unique \(z\) satisfying \(\mathsf V_{\tau}\); on a negative target cell, choose \(\theta^0,\theta^1\) satisfying \(\mathsf W_{\tau}\), by Thom encodings over the real closure of the ordered field generated by \((\mathbf p,\mathbf s_Y)\). The extracted coordinates are algebraic over the relevant ordered input field and are real algebraic over \(\mathbb Q\) when every supplied coordinate is rational or real algebraic. No operation on an arbitrary unencoded observed cell or score value is defined.
defs.def:response-polynomial-fiber:
Let
\[
L_{\mathcal G}=\left|\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\right|,
\qquad
K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)=L_{\mathcal G}+|\mathcal X_A|(|\mathcal X_Y|-1),
\qquad
\mathcal J=\mathcal E^{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal G)\sqcup\mathcal V\sqcup\mathcal R.
\]
The integer \(K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\) is a universal factorwise upper bound, not a claimed sharp support size. For \(g\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}\) introduce \(\gamma_g\), and for \(h\in\mathcal J\) and \(1\leq k\leq K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\) introduce \(\rho_{h,k}\). For a full cell \((v,r)\), define
\[
p_{v,r}(\theta)=
\sum_{g\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}}
\sum_{u\in\{1,\ldots,K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\}^{\mathcal J}}
\mathbf 1\{g(u)=(v,r)\}\gamma_g\prod_{h\in\mathcal J}\rho_{h,u_h},
\qquad
p_o(\theta)=\sum_{(v,r):\operatorname{proxy}(v,r)=o}p_{v,r}(\theta).
\]
Define \(q_{a,y}(\theta)\) by the same product sum after replacing the selected equation for \(A\) by the constant \(a\). With formal observed coordinates \(\mathbf p=(p_o)_o\), set
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p):={}&
\bigwedge_{g\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}}(\gamma_g^2-\gamma_g=0)
\ \wedge\ \sum_g\gamma_g=1\\
&\wedge\bigwedge_{h\in\mathcal J}
\left(\bigwedge_{k=1}^{K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)}\rho_{h,k}\geq0
\ \wedge\ \sum_{k=1}^{K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)}\rho_{h,k}=1\right)\\
&\wedge\bigwedge_{(v,r)}p_{v,r}(\theta)>0
\ \wedge\ \bigwedge_{o\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}}p_o(\theta)=p_o.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus every individual bidirected-edge or private factor has its own simplex and the joint latent law is the product over \(h\). The one-hot equations select one graph-wide tuple of label-compatible deterministic tables; they do not mix structural tables through an additional unrestricted district latent.
defs.def:symbolic-observed-partition:
Conjoin the simplex formula \(p_o\geq0\), \(\sum_op_o=1\), and the feasible-projection formula \(\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\) with every quantifier-free output of \(\mathsf I_{a,y}\), refine their common sign-invariant CAD, and discard infeasible cells. The remaining pairwise-disjoint formulas \(\psi_1(\mathbf p),\ldots,\psi_J(\mathbf p)\) form the coordinate partition \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\). Each coordinate cell stores, for every \((a,y)\), either \(\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p,z)\) or \(\mathsf W_j(\mathbf p,a,y,\theta^0,\theta^1)\).

Independently introduce the formal score coordinates \(\mathbf s=(s_y:y\in\mathcal X_Y)\). Conjoin the lifted coordinate-cell formulas with the quantifier-free output of \(\mathsf I_{\tau}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\), refine by one common sign-invariant CAD in \((\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\), and discard points whose \(\mathbf p\)-coordinate is infeasible. The resulting pairwise-disjoint formulas \(\chi_1(\mathbf p,\mathbf s),\ldots,\chi_K(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\) form
\[
\mathscr P^{\tau}_{\mathcal G,A,Y}
\quad\text{on}\quad
\{\mathbf p:\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\}
\times\mathbb R^{\mathcal X_Y}.
\]
This target partition refines the lift of the coordinate partition. Each target cell stores either the unique-value relation \(\mathsf V_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s,z)\) or the witness relation \(\mathsf W_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s,\theta^0,\theta^1)\). Thus coordinate negativity and target negativity are recorded separately.
defs.def:tcf-procedure:
On formal input \((\mathcal G,A,Y,\mathbf p)\), first construct the response-polynomial feasibility formula \(\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\), all coordinate-constancy formulas \(\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p)\), and the direct target-constancy formula \(\mathsf I_{\tau}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\) with \(\mathbf s\) retained as a formal real vector. Run one signed-subresultant CAD for the coordinate family in \(\mathbf p\), and a second signed-subresultant CAD for the target family in \((\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\) together with the lifted coordinate-cell polynomials. This produces the canonical coordinate cells \(\psi_j\) and target cells \(\chi_k\), with their respective unique-value or witness relations, before any fixing trace is enumerated.

After both base partitions have been fixed, enumerate expression-discovery traces. Start from every supported observed margin and partial-context trace kernel written as a rational expression in \(\mathbf p\). Recursively branch only by strict ancestral marginalization, restriction to a proper child of a nontrivial district decomposition, a licensed \(\Phi_v^{\lambda}\) update, or a delayed \(\Sigma_{c'}\) update that strictly extends the partial context. Retain the complete operation word and memoize only literal complete tuples \(\kappa=(\mathcal H,F,c,q,\pi,\Lambda)\), including the syntax of \(q\), \(\pi\), and every provenance entry in \(\Lambda\). An adjacent-swap optimization may merge branches only after replaying both license orders from their common pre-swap state in a fixed canonical order and verifying literal equality of the complete resulting tuples. Fixing and selection are never commuted.

For a candidate coordinate expression \(r(\mathbf p)=N(\mathbf p)/D(\mathbf p)\), a coordinate cell \(\psi_j\), and \((a,y)\) having a unique relation, decide
\[
\forall\mathbf p\,\forall z
\left[
\psi_j(\mathbf p)\wedge\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p,z)
\Longrightarrow
D(\mathbf p)\neq0\wedge D(\mathbf p)z=N(\mathbf p)
\right].
\]
For a candidate direct-target expression \(r_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)=N_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)/D_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\), formed as a score-linear combination of compatible trace expressions, and a target cell \(\chi_k\) having a unique relation, decide
\[
\forall\mathbf p\,\forall\mathbf s\,\forall z
\left[
\chi_k(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\wedge\mathsf V_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s,z)
\Longrightarrow
D_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\neq0
\wedge D_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)z=N_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)
\right].
\]
Annotate a cell only when its implication is true. If no candidate passes, retain the corresponding unique-value graph; on a nonconstant coordinate or target cell retain \(\mathsf W_j\) or \(\mathsf W_{\tau}\), respectively. Trace enumeration and annotation never split, merge, or otherwise alter either base partition. The notation \(\operatorname{TCF}(\mathcal G,A,Y,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) denotes the two symbolic partitions and their verified annotations, with formal names \(p_o=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o)\); a supplied \(s_Y\) selects the target-score section only at mathematical or exact specialization. The procedure neither names nor returns a colored hedge.
defs.def:terminal-qe-test:
For every \(a\in\mathcal X_A\) and \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), use disjoint copies \(\theta^0=(\gamma^0,\rho^0)\) and \(\theta^1=(\gamma^1,\rho^1)\) and eliminate precisely those response variables from
\[
\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p):=
\neg\exists\theta^0\,\exists\theta^1
\left[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^0;\mathbf p)
\wedge\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^1;\mathbf p)
\wedge q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1)
\right].
\]
The only free variables in this coordinate formula are the \(|\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}|\) coordinates \(\mathbf p\). On its true region define
\[
\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p,z):=
\exists\theta
\left[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)
\wedge z=q_{a,y}(\theta)
\right],
\]
and on its false region use the unnegated doubled conjunction \(\mathsf W_j(\mathbf p,a,y,\theta^0,\theta^1)\).

For a formal real score vector \(\mathbf s=(s_y:y\in\mathcal X_Y)\), define the target polynomial
\[
t_{\mathbf s}(\theta)
=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_y
\{q_{a_1,y}(\theta)-q_{a_0,y}(\theta)\}
\]
and the direct target-constancy formula
\[
\mathsf I_{\tau}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p,\mathbf s):=
\neg\exists\theta^0\,\exists\theta^1
\left[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^0;\mathbf p)
\wedge\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^1;\mathbf p)
\wedge t_{\mathbf s}(\theta^0)\neq t_{\mathbf s}(\theta^1)
\right].
\]
Its only free variables are \((\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\). On its true region define
\[
\mathsf V_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s,z):=
\exists\theta
\left[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)
\wedge z=t_{\mathbf s}(\theta)
\right],
\]
and on its false region define
\[
\mathsf W_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s,\theta^0,\theta^1):=
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^0;\mathbf p)
\wedge\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^1;\mathbf p)
\wedge t_{\mathbf s}(\theta^0)\neq t_{\mathbf s}(\theta^1).
\]
Quantifier elimination returns quantifier-free polynomial-sign formulas in the displayed free variables. No rationality or algebraicity is imposed on a supplied score map for the mathematical constancy assertion; represented point extraction is deferred to exact specialization.
defs.def:termination-budget:
For the size quantities \((n,\ell,c,h,g,K_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G),p_{\mathrm{coord}},p_{\tau},p_{\max},s)\), define
\[
L_{\mathrm{op}}=2^{n+1}+n(\ell+1)+c+1,
\qquad
B_{\mathrm{state}}=2^n c\sum_{j=0}^{2n}L_{\mathrm{op}}^j.
\]
Here \(2^n c\) bounds the initial observed-margin and partial-context traces, and the operation alphabet bounds ancestral and district subset choices, vertex-license choices, strict context extensions, and one harmless terminal marker. The recursive word length \(2n\) counts every provenance-bearing marginalization, district restriction, fixing, and selection in its actual order.

Let
\[
p_{\mathrm{coord}}
=2\{g+hK_{\mathrm{ub}}(\mathcal G)\}+|\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}|,
\qquad
p_{\tau}=p_{\mathrm{coord}}+|\mathcal X_Y|,
\qquad
p_{\max}=p_{\tau}.
\]
Let \(s\) be the maximum of the complete binary encoding lengths of the trace-independent coordinate-CAD input, the trace-independent target-CAD input, and any one coordinate or target whole-cell candidate-verification sentence generated by an operation word of length at most \(2n\). The length includes canonical cell formulas, cleared numerators and denominators, polynomial counts, degrees, integer coefficients, variable indices, Boolean connectives, free observed-cell names, and free score-coordinate names. Define
\[
C_{\mathrm{coord}}=\operatorname{CAD}(p_{\mathrm{coord}},s),
\qquad
C_{\tau}=\operatorname{CAD}(p_{\tau},s),
\qquad
C_{\mathrm{base}}=C_{\mathrm{coord}}+C_{\tau},
\]
\[
N_{\mathrm{check}}
=B_{\mathrm{state}}
\left\{|\mathcal X_A||\mathcal X_Y|C_{\mathrm{coord}}+C_{\tau}\right\},
\]
and
\[
B_{\mathrm{tot}}
=B_{\mathrm{state}}+C_{\mathrm{base}}
+N_{\mathrm{check}}\operatorname{CAD}(p_{\max}+1,s).
\]
The two base CADs are run once each before trace enumeration. Their combined number of projection, real-root-isolation, sign-evaluation steps and output cells is at most \(C_{\mathrm{base}}\). Each later annotation sentence has at most one response vector, \(z\), the free observed coordinates, and, for a target check, the free score coordinates; hence it has at most \(p_{\max}+1\) variables. Exact coordinate specialization under \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) and exact target specialization under \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},s_Y)\) are separate finite sign computations.

thm:qe-failure-compiler.proof_tex:
Because \(\omega\) satisfies \(\mathsf W_j\), \(\text{def:terminal-qe-test}\) and \(\text{def:symbolic-observed-partition}\) give
\[
\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^i;P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\quad(i=0,1),
\qquad
q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1).
\tag{1}
\]
Applying \(\text{lem:negative-cell-model-pair}\) to (1) yields
\[
\begin{gathered}
\mathcal M_i\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}),
\qquad
P_{\mathcal M_i}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}},\\
Q_a^{\mathcal M_i}(y)=q_{a,y}(\theta^i),
\qquad i=0,1.
\end{gathered}
\tag{2}
\]
That lemma also proves that each decoded latent law is a product over the individual bidirected-edge and private factors and that every full-data cell is strictly positive.  Substitution of (2) into (1) gives
\[
Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(y)\neq Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(y).
\tag{3}
\]

It remains to verify the algorithmic assertions.  The history \(\mathcal T\) and graph \(\mathcal G\) are finite, so there are finitely many prefixes and finitely many choices of \((\kappa_*,D,D')\) examined in the fixed order of \(\text{def:certificate-compiler}\).  Every ancestor, district, root, inclusion, and intervention-incidence conjunct of \(\Delta\) is decidable by inspection of a finite graph.  A stored trace is a rational expression in observed cells and response coordinates.  Each denominator that the compiler clears is supported on its recorded pre-restriction trace.  By the strict full-cell inequalities in (1), every required marginal or selected cell is a finite sum of positive cells and is therefore nonzero.  Multiplying by the finite product of these nonzero denominators consequently turns each trace equality or inequality into an equivalent polynomial sign condition.

By \(\text{def:exact-observed-specialization}\), the coordinates of \(\theta^0,\theta^1\) have Thom encodings over the real closure of the ordered field generated by \(\mathbf p=(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o))_o\).  The signed-subresultant comparisons stipulated in \(\text{def:certificate-compiler}\) reduce each polynomial comparison at these encodings to finitely many signs at \(\mathbf p\), and \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) decides those signs.  Thus every candidate test terminates.  A finite deterministic enumeration whose individual tests terminate either returns the first triple satisfying every conjunct of \(\Delta\), or reaches its end, in which case no enumerated triple satisfies all conjuncts.  These are precisely the two advertised tags.  In either case the returned models are the pair in (2), so (2)--(3) establish the model claims independently of the tag.  The argument never infers colored-hedge membership, forest realization, or alignment with a graphwise recursion failure.

thm:colored-completeness.proof_tex:
By \(\text{thm:tcf-termination}\), the two trace-independent base constructions and the subsequent finite trace-annotation phase terminate.  By \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy}\), the coordinate cells partition the feasible observed-law projection and the target cells partition its product with the unrestricted real score coordinates.  The construction in \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\) fixes both partitions before trace enumeration and admits an annotation only after its whole-cell equality sentence has been verified.  Thus trace discovery can neither split nor merge a base cell.

Fix a compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and a real score map \(s_Y\), and write
\[
\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}}=(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o))_o,
\qquad
\mathbf s_Y=(s_Y(y))_y.
\]
Compatibility makes \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) nonempty.  The dichotomy lemma gives unique coordinate and target cells and proves
\[
\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal M\mapsto Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
\text{ is constant on }\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}),
\tag{1}
\]
and
\[
\mathsf I_\tau(\mathcal G;\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}},\mathbf s_Y)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal M\mapsto\tau_{s_Y}^{\mathcal M}
\text{ is constant on }\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{2}
\]

Suppose (1) holds.  Its coordinate value relation is nonempty and single-valued.  If a rational trace \(N/D\) passes the whole-cell check, \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\) proves \(D(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})\neq0\) and \(D(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)=N(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}})\) for every model in the fiber; otherwise the unique-value graph is retained.  In either case \(\text{thm:tcf-soundness}\) gives
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
\quad\text{for every }\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{3}
\]
Conversely, a common identifying value in (3) makes the right side constant, and (1) holds.  This proves the coordinate iff.

The same argument applies directly to (2), without assuming coordinatewise constancy.  If the target cell retains \(\mathsf V_\tau\), its unique-value semantics and the response-fiber equality in \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy}\) give the causal contrast.  If it has a rational annotation \(N_\tau/D_\tau\), the target whole-cell implication in \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\) gives
\[
D_\tau(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}},\mathbf s_Y)\neq0,
\qquad
D_\tau(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}},\mathbf s_Y)\tau_{s_Y}^{\mathcal M}
=N_\tau(\mathbf p_{\mathrm{obs}},\mathbf s_Y)
\tag{4}
\]
for every model in the fiber.  Therefore, exactly when (2) holds,
\[
f_{\tau,k}(P_{\mathrm{obs}};s_Y)=\tau_{s_Y}^{\mathcal M}
\quad\text{for every }\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{5}
\]
This establishes the direct target iff even when some interventional coordinates vary and cancel in the score contrast.

If a coordinate test fails, the coordinate clause of the dichotomy lemma supplies a satisfiable \(\mathsf W_j\) and two strictly positive individual-edge-factorized models in the same observed fiber with different coordinate values.  If the target test fails, its target clause supplies a satisfiable \(\mathsf W_\tau\) and models \(\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\) satisfying
\[
P_{\mathcal M_0}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathcal M_1}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}},
\qquad
\tau_{s_Y}^{\mathcal M_0}\neq\tau_{s_Y}^{\mathcal M_1}.
\tag{6}
\]
These are ordinary existential consequences of a nonconstant real response fiber, so no exact encoding is required.  By \(\text{prop:ambient-nonrecovery-transfer}\), each pair also proves nonidentification in the larger published ambient fiber.  If \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) is supplied, coordinate witnesses are represented and \(\text{thm:qe-failure-compiler}\) terminates with a checked divergence record or exhaustion.  If \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},s_Y)\) is supplied, \(\text{def:exact-observed-specialization}\) represents the target pair.  No step turns either diagnostic tag into a colored hedge.

Finally, if every coordinate at \(a_0\) and \(a_1\) is constant, finiteness of \(\mathcal X_Y\) permits termwise substitution of (3) into \(\text{def:causal-query}\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_{s_Y}^{\mathcal M}
&=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)
\{Q_{a_1}^{\mathcal M}(y)-Q_{a_0}^{\mathcal M}(y)\}\\
&=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)
\{f_{a_1,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)-f_{a_0,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
Equation (7) is the additional sufficient coordinatewise formula; the iff in (2)--(5) is the direct target criterion.  Equations (1)--(7), together with the finite partitions and termination already established, prove the theorem with no graphwise colored-hedge claim.

prop:eipfd-star-worked.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G_\star)\).  Apply \(\text{lem:eipfd-frontdoor-identification}\) with \(H=\{C\}\) and \(m=1\).  Membership in the displayed positive class supplies the lemma's strict-positivity premise, so every conditioning event in the following finite sums has a positive denominator.  The lemma gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
&=\sum_{c\in\mathcal X_C}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(c)
\sum_{b\in\mathcal X_{B_1}}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(b\mid a,c,R_W=0)\\
&\qquad\times\sum_{a'\in\mathcal X_A}
P_{\mathrm{obs}}(y\mid b,a',c,R_W=0)
P_{\mathrm{obs}}(a'\mid c,R_W=0)\\
&=f_a^\star(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y),
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]
where the last equality is \(\text{def:eipfd-star-functional}\). We next check the two comparator premises.  By \(\text{def:endogenous-proxy-frontdoor-class}\), the edge \(A\leftrightarrow Y\) occurs in \(\mathcal G_\star\). \[

\tag{2}
\]

\[
\neg\operatorname{RC}(\mathcal G_\star,A,Y).
\tag{3}
\]

The right side of (1) depends only on \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and equals the causal coordinate for every model in its fiber.  Hence the coordinate is constant on the fiber.  By \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy}\), the unique TCF coordinate cell is identifying, and by \(\text{thm:tcf-soundness}\) its carried value is the common value in (1). defs.def:tcf-procedure:
On formal input \((\mathcal G,A,Y,\mathbf p)\), first construct the response-polynomial feasibility formula \(\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\), all coordinate-constancy formulas \(\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p)\), and the direct target-constancy formula \(\mathsf I_{\tau}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\) with \(\mathbf s\) retained as a formal real vector. Run one signed-subresultant CAD for the coordinate family in \(\mathbf p\), and a second signed-subresultant CAD for the target family in \((\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\) together with the lifted coordinate-cell polynomials. This produces the canonical coordinate cells \(\psi_j\) and target cells \(\chi_k\), with their respective unique-value or witness relations, before any fixing trace is enumerated.

After both base partitions have been fixed, enumerate expression-discovery traces. Start from every supported observed margin and partial-context trace kernel written as a rational expression in \(\mathbf p\). Recursively branch only by strict ancestral marginalization, restriction to a proper child of a nontrivial district decomposition, a licensed \(\Phi_v^{\lambda}\) update, or a delayed \(\Sigma_{c'}\) update that strictly extends the partial context. Retain the complete operation word and memoize only literal complete tuples \(\kappa=(\mathcal H,F,c,q,\pi,\Lambda)\), including the syntax of \(q\), \(\pi\), and every provenance entry in \(\Lambda\). An adjacent-swap optimization may merge branches only after replaying both license orders from their common pre-swap state in a fixed canonical order and verifying literal equality of the complete resulting tuples. Fixing and selection are never commuted.

For a candidate coordinate expression \(r(\mathbf p)=N(\mathbf p)/D(\mathbf p)\), a coordinate cell \(\psi_j\), and \((a,y)\) having a unique relation, decide
\[
\forall\mathbf p\,\forall z
\left[
\psi_j(\mathbf p)\wedge\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p,z)
\Longrightarrow
D(\mathbf p)\neq0\wedge D(\mathbf p)z=N(\mathbf p)
\right].
\]
For a candidate direct-target expression \(r_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)=N_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)/D_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\), formed as a score-linear combination of compatible trace expressions, and a target cell \(\chi_k\) having a unique relation, decide
\[
\forall\mathbf p\,\forall\mathbf s\,\forall z
\left[
\chi_k(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\wedge\mathsf V_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s,z)
\Longrightarrow
D_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\neq0
\wedge D_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)z=N_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)
\right].
\]
Annotate a cell only when its implication is true. If no candidate passes, retain the corresponding unique-value graph; on a nonconstant coordinate or target cell retain \(\mathsf W_j\) or \(\mathsf W_{\tau}\), respectively. Trace enumeration and annotation never split, merge, or otherwise alter either base partition. The procedure neither names nor returns a colored hedge.

thm:two-comparator-strict-extension.proof_tex:
Let \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) be compatible with the common finite, strictly positive regular-maximal class, fix \((a,y)\), and let \(\psi_j\) be its unique TCF coordinate cell.  For \(\xi\in\operatorname{DA4}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\), \(\text{lem:da4-recovery}\) gives
\[
f^{\mathrm{DA4}}_{a,\xi}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)
=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
\quad\text{for every }\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{1}
\]
The left side depends only on the observed law, so the causal coordinate is constant on the fiber.  By \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy}\), \(\psi_j\) is identifying, and \(\text{thm:tcf-soundness}\) yields
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).
\tag{2}
\]
Combining (1)--(2) gives
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)
=f^{\mathrm{DA4}}_{a,\xi}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y).
\tag{3}
\]

If \(\operatorname{RC}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) holds, \(\text{lem:root-control-context-recovery}\) analogously gives
\[
f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)
=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
\quad\text{for every }\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{4}
\]
The same constancy, dichotomy, and soundness argument proves
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y).
\tag{5}
\]
Equations (3) and (5) use only the common finite positive domain and therefore establish, respectively, containment of the de Aguas criterion and embedding of the root-control result on that domain.

For strictness of the first containment, fix \(\mathcal G(H,m)\in\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{EIPFD}}\).  By \(\text{def:endogenous-proxy-frontdoor-class}\), it contains \(A\leftrightarrow Y\).  This bidirected length-one path survives deletion of directed arrows out of \(A\), and no conditioning vertex can block it.  Thus condition \(\mathrm{(v)}\) of every proposed de Aguas certificate fails, so
\[
\operatorname{DA4}(\mathcal G(H,m),A,Y)=\varnothing.
\tag{6}
\]
On the other hand, \(\text{lem:eipfd-frontdoor-identification}\) gives, for every model in the nonempty fiber,
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
&=\sum_hP_{\mathrm{obs}}(h)
\sum_{b\in\mathcal X_{B_1}}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(b\mid a,h,R_W=0)\\
&\qquad\times\sum_{a'\in\mathcal X_A}
P_{\mathrm{obs}}(y\mid b,a',h,R_W=0)
P_{\mathrm{obs}}(a'\mid h,R_W=0).
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
Strict full-data positivity makes every displayed conditional denominator positive.  The right side is an observed-law functional, so the coordinate is constant on the fiber.  The dichotomy lemma and TCF soundness therefore show that the TCF cell carries (7).  Equations (6)--(7) exhibit a whole TCF-identified family outside the de Aguas certificate domain, proving strict class-relative extension.

Every member of the family also contains \(C\to R_W\), so the label-context variable \(R_W\) is not an observed causal root.  The premise of \(\operatorname{RC}\) is therefore inapplicable to this family; this is not a strictness assertion about the complete root-control domain.  When \(H=\{C\}\) and \(m=1\), \(\text{prop:eipfd-star-worked}\) identifies (7) term by term with \(f_a^\star(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\), completing the proof.

prop:ordinary-id-reduction.proof_tex:
Assume \(\mathcal R=\varnothing\), \(\mathcal V^{\dagger}=\varnothing\), and the label set is empty.  There is then one empty context, no context-selection transition, and no nontrivial license.  The observed record is the substantive record.  Unfolding \(\text{def:trace-state}\) and \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\), the graphical transitions reduce to ancestral marginalization, district decomposition, and uncolored fixing.  These are precisely the ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}\) transitions, while the color, context, and license-trace components remain vacuous.  Induction on the operation word therefore proves that every rational graphical trace returned by TCF is the corresponding ordinary fixing expression.

Suppose ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}\) returns \(f_a^{\mathrm{ID}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\).  By \(\text{lem:ordinary-id-soundness}\),
\[
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
=f_a^{\mathrm{ID}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)
\quad\text{for every }\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{1}
\]
Thus the coordinate is constant on the fiber.  By \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy}\), the unique TCF coordinate cell is identifying.  The first paragraph shows that the ordinary expression is an enumerated TCF candidate, and (1), which is uniform over every compatible law for this graph, verifies its whole-cell equality.  Hence the annotation test in \(\text{def:tcf-procedure}\) accepts it.  Applying \(\text{thm:tcf-soundness}\) gives
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)
=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
=f_a^{\mathrm{ID}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y).
\tag{2}
\]
The ordinary ID statement is graphwise, whereas the semialgebraic constancy test may identify a coordinate only at a special observed law.  Therefore (1)--(2) establish the claimed one-way reduction and no converse or hedge-compiler conclusion.

defs.def:tcf-procedure:
On formal input \((\mathcal G,A,Y,\mathbf p)\), first construct the response-polynomial feasibility formula \(\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\), all coordinate-constancy formulas \(\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p)\), and the direct target-constancy formula \(\mathsf I_{\tau}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\) with \(\mathbf s\) retained as a formal real vector. Run one signed-subresultant CAD for the coordinate family in \(\mathbf p\), and a second signed-subresultant CAD for the target family in \((\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\) together with the lifted coordinate-cell polynomials. This produces the canonical coordinate cells \(\psi_j\) and target cells \(\chi_k\), with their respective unique-value or witness relations, before any fixing trace is enumerated.

After both base partitions have been fixed, enumerate expression-discovery traces. Start from every supported observed margin and partial-context trace kernel written as a rational expression in \(\mathbf p\). Recursively branch only by strict ancestral marginalization, restriction to a proper child of a nontrivial district decomposition, a licensed \(\Phi_v^{\lambda}\) update, or a delayed \(\Sigma_{c'}\) update that strictly extends the partial context. Retain the complete operation word and memoize only literal complete tuples \(\kappa=(\mathcal H,F,c,q,\pi,\Lambda)\), including the syntax of \(q\), \(\pi\), and every provenance entry in \(\Lambda\). An adjacent-swap optimization may merge branches only after replaying both license orders from their common pre-swap state in a fixed canonical order and verifying literal equality of the complete resulting tuples. Fixing and selection are never commuted.

For a candidate coordinate expression \(r(\mathbf p)=N(\mathbf p)/D(\mathbf p)\), a coordinate cell \(\psi_j\), and \((a,y)\) having a unique relation, decide
\[
\forall\mathbf p\,\forall z
\left[
\psi_j(\mathbf p)\wedge\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p,z)
\Longrightarrow
D(\mathbf p)\neq0\wedge D(\mathbf p)z=N(\mathbf p)
\right].
\]
For a candidate direct-target expression \(r_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)=N_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)/D_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\), formed as a score-linear combination of compatible trace expressions, and a target cell \(\chi_k\) having a unique relation, decide
\[
\forall\mathbf p\,\forall\mathbf s\,\forall z
\left[
\chi_k(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\wedge\mathsf V_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s,z)
\Longrightarrow
D_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)\neq0
\wedge D_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)z=N_{\tau}(\mathbf p,\mathbf s)
\right].
\]
Annotate a cell only when its implication is true. If no candidate passes, retain the corresponding unique-value graph; on a nonconstant coordinate or target cell retain \(\mathsf W_j\) or \(\mathsf W_{\tau}\), respectively. Trace enumeration and annotation never split, merge, or otherwise alter either base partition. The notation \(\operatorname{TCF}(\mathcal G,A,Y,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) denotes the two symbolic partitions and their verified annotations, with formal names \(p_o=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o)\); a supplied \(s_Y\) selects the target-score section only at mathematical or exact specialization. The procedure neither names nor returns a colored hedge.
defs.def:trace-state: \(\kappa=(\mathcal H,F,c,q,\pi,\Lambda)\), where \(\mathcal H\) is the current CADMG, \(F\) is its fixed set, \(c\) is a partial assignment to missingness indicators, \(q\) is a normalized kernel on the random vertices of \(\mathcal H\), \(\pi\) is a finite expression in observed cells of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), and \(\Lambda\) is an ordered list of pairs consisting of a label license and the pre-restriction trace that licensed it.

thm:root-control-reduction.proof_tex:
Assume \(\operatorname{RC}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) and that every context graph is identifying.  By \(\text{def:root-control-functional}\), each label-context variable is observed and parentless.  Its structural equation therefore has no endogenous parent, and intervention on \(A\) cannot change its distribution.  Hence, for every context value \(c\),
\[
P_{\mathcal M}(C=c\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))
=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(C=c).
\tag{1}
\]
The recovery theorem \(\text{lem:root-control-context-recovery}\) supplies a sound functional in each context and the aggregation identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
&=\sum_cP_{\mathrm{obs}}(C=c)
f^{\mathrm{ID}}_{a,c}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\\
&=f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
for every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  On the finite positive class, every context occurring in a conditional expression is supported; a zero-weight term in the published aggregation, if present syntactically, contributes zero and requires no division.

Because the context variables are roots, restricting their values before the context-specific ID operations cannot remove a parent mechanism or a pre-restriction license needed later.  Thus delayed restriction contributes no additional identifying information in this regime.  More formally, (2) is already an observed-law functional common to the whole fiber, so \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy}\) makes the unique TCF coordinate cell identifying, and \(\text{thm:tcf-soundness}\) gives
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)
=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
=f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y).
\tag{3}
\]
The cited root-control result is uniform over its graph class, while TCF tests constancy at each observed law.  Therefore (3) proves the reduction but not the excluded converse for an exceptional law.

thm:binary-witness-observed-support-obst.proof_tex:
We give an explicit finite counterexample and then prove the two support assertions.

Let \(\mathcal V=\{A,Y,Z\}\), let \(\mathcal R=\varnothing\), let \(\mathcal X_A=\mathcal X_Y=\{0,1\}\), and let \(\mathcal X_Z=\{0,1,2\}\). Thus every substantive variable is always observed and \(\mathcal O=(A,Y,Z)\). Let \(\mathcal G\) have the directed edge \(A\to Y\), the bidirected edge \(A\leftrightarrow Y\), the isolated vertex \(Z\), and the empty label set. Its directed part is acyclic, as required by \(\mathrm{ass{:}acyclic}\). Because \(\mathcal R=\varnothing\), there is no missingness context in which a label could occur; consequently the empty label set is regular and maximal, as required by \(\mathrm{ass{:}regular}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}maximal}\). Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}proxy\text{-}consistency}\) is vacuous for this graph.

Let \(\mathcal F\) be the \(C\)-forest induced by \(\{A,Y\}\), and let \(\mathcal F'\) be its subforest induced by \(\{Y\}\). The forest \(\mathcal F\) is bidirected-connected, \(A\) has the unique directed child \(Y\), and \(Y\) has no directed child, so its root set is \(\{Y\}\); \(\mathcal F'\) has the same root set. Moreover,
\[
 \mathcal F\cap\{A\}=\{A\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal F'\cap\{A\}=\varnothing.
\]
The common root \(Y\) is an ancestor of \(Y\) after intervention on \(A\), since a vertex is its own ancestor. Take the empty color assignment and the trace family consisting only of the empty trace. This trace family is prefix closed, and the licensing condition is vacuous because no color occurs. Hence, by \(\mathrm{def{:}colored\text{-}hedge}\),
\[
 H=(\mathcal F,\mathcal F',\varnothing,\{\varnothing\})
 \in \operatorname{CH}(\mathcal G,A,Y).
\]

We next construct two compatible models. Let \(U\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) be the exogenous factor shared by \(A\) and \(Y\). Independently, let \(E_A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/4)\), let \(E_Y\) be uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,16\}\), and let \(E_Z\) be uniform on \(\{0,1,2\}\). Put
\[
 A=U\mathbin{\oplus}E_A,
 \qquad
 Z=E_Z,
 \qquad
 t_0=\frac14,
 \qquad
 t_1=-\frac14,
\]
where \(\oplus\) denotes addition modulo two and the Bernoulli parameter is the probability of value one. For \(i\in\{0,1\}\), define
\[
 k_i(u,a)
 =16\left[\frac12+t_i\left\{\mathbf 1(u=a)-\frac34\right\}\right],
\]
and in model \(\mathcal M_i\) set
\[
 Y=\mathbf 1\{E_Y\leq k_i(U,A)\}.
\]
These are deterministic finite response tables because the thresholds are integers: \(k_0(u,a)\) is \(9\) when \(u=a\) and \(5\) otherwise, whereas \(k_1(u,a)\) is \(7\) when \(u=a\) and \(11\) otherwise. For each model, the equation for \(A\) depends on the shared factor \(U\), while the equation for \(Y\) depends on both \(A\) and \(U\), because changing the truth value of \(u=a\) changes the threshold. Thus the directed edge \(A\to Y\) and the individual bidirected-edge factor for \(A\leftrightarrow Y\) are active, and no additional edge is introduced. The factors \(U,E_A,E_Y,E_Z\) are mutually independent, so \(\mathrm{ass{:}semimarkovian}\) holds. The empty label set imposes no response-table restriction.

For positivity, define
\[
 \pi_i(u,a)=\frac{k_i(u,a)}{16}.
\]
The displayed threshold values give \(0<\pi_i(u,a)<1\) for every \(i,u,a\). Moreover, \(P(E_A=e)>0\) for both \(e\in\{0,1\}\). Therefore, for every \((a,y,z)\in\mathcal X_A\times\mathcal X_Y\times\mathcal X_Z\), independence and the structural equations give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a,Y=y,Z=z)
 &=\frac13\sum_{u=0}^1
 \frac12 P(E_A=a\mathbin{\oplus}u)
 \pi_i(u,a)^y\{1-\pi_i(u,a)\}^{1-y}\\
 &>0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This verifies \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}positivity}\) cell by cell. All alphabets are finite, as required by \(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\text{-}alphabets}\). The graph conditions established above and \(\mathrm{def{:}positive\text{-}rm\text{-}class}\) therefore imply
\[
 \mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1
 \in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G).
\]

We now compute the observed laws. For either \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a)
 =\sum_{u=0}^1\frac12P(E_A=a\mathbin{\oplus}u)
 =\frac12\left(\frac34+\frac14\right)
 =\frac12,
\]
and
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(U=a,A=a)
 =P(U=a,E_A=0)
 =\frac12\cdot\frac34
 =\frac38.
\]
Division is legitimate because \(P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a)=1/2>0\), and hence
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(U=a\mid A=a)
 =\frac{3/8}{1/2}
 =\frac34.
\]
Using the response equation for \(Y\) and the conditional law of total probability,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(Y=1\mid A=a)
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
 \left[\frac12+t_i\left\{\mathbf 1(u=a)-\frac34\right\}\right]
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(U=u\mid A=a)\\
 &=\frac12+t_i\left\{P_{\mathcal M_i}(U=a\mid A=a)-\frac34\right\}\\
 &=\frac12.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Since \(Z=E_Z\) is independent and uniform, both models consequently induce
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a,Y=y,Z=z)
 =\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac13
 =\frac1{12}
\]
for every observed cell. Let \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) denote this common uniform, and hence strictly positive, observed law.

Under \(\operatorname{do}(A=a)\), the structural intervention in \(\mathrm{def{:}causal\text{-}query}\) replaces the equation for \(A\) by the constant \(a\) and leaves the exogenous distribution, in particular \(U\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), unchanged. Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_a^{\mathcal M_i}(1)
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
 \left[\frac12+t_i\left\{\mathbf 1(u=a)-\frac34\right\}\right]P(U=u)\\
 &=\frac12+t_i\left(\frac12-\frac34\right)\\
 &=\frac12-\frac{t_i}{4}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
It follows that
\[
 Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(1)=\frac7{16},
 \qquad
 Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(1)=\frac9{16}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}observational\text{-}fiber}\), both models lie in \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), but their interventional laws differ. Thus the displayed colored hedge has two strictly positive observationally equivalent witnesses with different \(Q_a\).

It remains to prove that no universal binary witness can match this observed law and to establish the general support claim. Let \(W\) be always observed and define
\[
 S_W=\{w:P_{\mathrm{obs}}(W=w)>0\}.
\]
In any model inducing \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), the observed value of \(W\) is its substantive value, so
\[
 S_W\subseteq\mathcal X_W
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 |\mathcal X_W|\geq |S_W|.
\]
For a partially observed substantive coordinate \(W\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}proxy\text{-}consistency}\) gives \(W^{\dagger}=W\) on \(R_W=1\). The required conditioning event has positive probability under \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}positivity}\): by \(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\text{-}alphabets}\), summing the finitely many positive full-data cells with \(R_W=1\) gives \(P_{\mathcal M}(R_W=1)>0\). Consequently
\[
 S_W^{\dagger}
 =\operatorname{supp}_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}(W^{\dagger}\mid R_W=1)
 \subseteq\mathcal X_W,
\]
and hence
\[
 |\mathcal X_W|\geq |S_W^{\dagger}|.
\]

Under \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}positivity}\), both inclusions are equalities at the level of supports. Indeed, for every \(w\in\mathcal X_W\), summing the positive full-data cells whose substantive coordinate is \(W=w\) yields
\[
 P_{\mathcal M}(W=w)>0
\]
when \(W\) is always observed. If \(W\) is partially observed, summing the positive full-data cells with \(W=w\) and \(R_W=1\) gives
\[
 P_{\mathcal M}(W=w,R_W=1)>0.
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass{:}proxy\text{-}consistency}\), this equals
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}(W^{\dagger}=w,R_W=1)>0.
\]
Thus every declared substantive value occurs in the conditional proxy support. Conversely, proxy consistency permits no value outside \(\mathcal X_W\) on \(R_W=1\). We have therefore proved
\[
 |S_W|=|\mathcal X_W|
 \quad\text{for always-observed }W,
 \qquad
 |S_W^{\dagger}|=|\mathcal X_W|
 \quad\text{for partially observed }W.
\]

In the constructed common law, \(S_Z=\{0,1,2\}\). Hence every model matching \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) must satisfy \(|\mathcal X_Z|\geq3\), so no such model can make every substantive variable binary. This disproves the universal binary-witness assertion.

Finally, for an arbitrary integer \(m\geq2\), replace \(\mathcal X_Z\) by \(\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\) and take \(E_Z\) uniform on it, leaving the equations for \(A\) and \(Y\) unchanged. The same computation gives two strictly positive models with a common observed law and distinct query values. The forests \(\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F\), their districts and roots, the empty coloring, and the trace family are unchanged because \(Z\) is isolated and belongs to neither forest. On the other hand, the observed support of \(Z\) has cardinality \(m\), so the support argument forces \(|\mathcal X_Z|\geq m\); the displayed construction attains equality. Thus the smallest required \(Z\)-alphabet coordinate is \(m\), while the colored hedge data are fixed. Since \(m\) is arbitrary, the smallest substantive alphabet vector is not determined by the color and district structure of a colored hedge alone. This proves every assertion of the theorem.

snapshot.stmt: The universal binary-witness assertion is false, and the smallest substantive alphabet vector is not determined by the color and district structure of a colored hedge alone. There exist a finite regular-maximal graph \(\mathcal G\), a hedge in \(\operatorname{CH}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\), and a strictly positive compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) for which two models in \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) have different \(Q_a\), but no model matching \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) can make every substantive variable binary. More generally, an always-observed substantive coordinate requires at least the cardinality of its observed support, and a partially observed coordinate \(Z\) requires at least \(|\operatorname{supp}(Z^{\dagger}\mid R_Z=1)|\). Under strict positivity these lower bounds equal the declared substantive alphabet cardinalities.

defs.def:binary-response-handle: Begin with the response-function cells indexed by \((\mathcal F,\mathcal F',\chi,T)\in\operatorname{CH}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\); impose the polynomial equalities for every observed proxy trace and every color deletion; then use label-preserving output randomization with parameter \(\varepsilon\) and alphabet lifting to search for a two-state substantive encoding without specifying its response tables in advance.
defs.def:causal-query: For \(a\in\mathcal X_A\), set \(Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)=P_{\mathcal M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))\), and set \(\tau_{s_Y}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)\{Q_{a_1}^{\mathcal M}(y)-Q_{a_0}^{\mathcal M}(y)\}\).
defs.def:colored-hedge: \(\operatorname{CH}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) is the set of tuples \((\mathcal F,\mathcal F',\chi,T)\) such that \(\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F\) are equally rooted \(C\)-forests, \(\mathcal F\cap A\neq\varnothing\), \(\mathcal F'\cap A=\varnothing\), their roots are ancestors of \(Y\) after intervention on \(A\), \(\chi\) assigns every label-sensitive edge its missingness context, and \(T\) is a prefix-closed collection of observed traces on which every color used by the two forests is licensed.
defs.def:observational-fiber: \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G):P_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}}\}\).
defs.def:positive-rm-class: \(\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G):|\mathcal X_Z|<\infty\text{ for every }Z\in\mathcal V\cup\mathcal R\cup\mathcal V^{\dagger},\ \mathcal G\text{ is regular and maximal},\ P_{\mathcal M}(v,r)>0\text{ for every }(v,r)\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\}\).

assumptions.ass:acyclic: The directed part of \(\mathcal G\) is acyclic.
assumptions.ass:finite-alphabets: \(|\mathcal X_Z|<\infty\) for every \(Z\in\mathcal V\cup\mathcal R\cup\mathcal V^{\dagger}\).
assumptions.ass:maximal: The label set of \(\mathcal G\) is maximal.
assumptions.ass:proxy-consistency: For every partially observed \(Z\in\mathcal V\), \(Z^{\dagger}=Z\) when \(R_Z=1\) and \(Z^{\dagger}=\star\) when \(R_Z=0\).
assumptions.ass:regular: The label set of \(\mathcal G\) is regular.
assumptions.ass:semimarkovian: \(\mathcal M\) has one exogenous factor shared by the two endpoints of each bidirected edge of \(\mathcal G\), one private exogenous factor for each substantive or missingness vertex, and all these factors are mutually independent.
assumptions.ass:strict-positivity: \(P_{\mathcal M}(v,r)>0\) for every \((v,r)\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\).
assumptions.ass:label-semantics: Every label \((X,Z,R_X=0)\) in \(\mathcal G\) encodes that the structural mechanism for \(Z\) omits \(X\) in context \(R_X=0\).
