These are deterministic finite response tables because the thresholds are integers: \(k_0(u,a)\) is \(9\) when \(u=a\) and \(5\) otherwise, whereas \(k_1(u,a)\) is \(7\) when \(u=a\) and \(11\) otherwise. For each model, the equation for \(A\) depends on the shared factor \(U\), while the equation for \(Y\) depends on both \(A\) and \(U\), because changing the truth value of \(u=a\) changes the threshold. Thus the directed edge \(A\to Y\) and the individual bidirected-edge factor for \(A\leftrightarrow Y\) are active, and no additional edge is introduced. The factors \(U,E_A,E_Y,E_Z\) are mutually independent, so \(\mathrm{ass{:}semimarkovian}\) holds. The empty label set imposes no response-table restriction.

For positivity, define
\[
 \pi_i(u,a)=\frac{k_i(u,a)}{16}.
\]
The displayed threshold values give \(0<\pi_i(u,a)<1\) for every \(i,u,a\). Moreover, \(P(E_A=e)>0\) for both \(e\in\{0,1\}\). Therefore, for every \((a,y,z)\in\mathcal X_A\times\mathcal X_Y\times\mathcal X_Z\), independence and the structural equations give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a,Y=y,Z=z)
 &=\frac13\sum_{u=0}^1
 \frac12 P(E_A=a\mathbin{\oplus}u)
 \pi_i(u,a)^y\{1-\pi_i(u,a)\}^{1-y}\\
 &>0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This verifies \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}positivity}\) cell by cell. All alphabets are finite, as required by \(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\text{-}alphabets}\). The graph conditions established above and \(\mathrm{def{:}positive\text{-}rm\text{-}class}\) therefore imply
\[
 \mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1
 \in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G).
\]

We now compute the observed laws. For either \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a)
 =\sum_{u=0}^1\frac12P(E_A=a\mathbin{\oplus}u)
 =\frac12\left(\frac34+\frac14\right)
 =\frac12,
\]
and
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(U=a,A=a)
 =P(U=a,E_A=0)
 =\frac12\cdot\frac34
 =\frac38.
\]
Division is legitimate because \(P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a)=1/2>0\), and hence
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(U=a\mid A=a)
 =\frac{3/8}{1/2}
 =\frac34.
\]
Using the response equation for \(Y\) and the conditional law of total probability,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(Y=1\mid A=a)
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
 \left[\frac12+t_i\left\{\mathbf 1(u=a)-\frac34\right\}\right]
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(U=u\mid A=a)\\
 &=\frac12+t_i\left\{P_{\mathcal M_i}(U=a\mid A=a)-\frac34\right\}\\
 &=\frac12.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Since \(Z=E_Z\) is independent and uniform, both models consequently induce
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a,Y=y,Z=z)
 =\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac13
 =\frac1{12}
\]
for every observed cell. Let \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) denote this common uniform, and hence strictly positive, observed law.

Under \(\operatorname{do}(A=a)\), the structural intervention in \(\mathrm{def{:}causal\text{-}query}\) replaces the equation for \(A\) by the constant \(a\) and leaves the exogenous distribution, in particular \(U\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), unchanged. Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_a^{\mathcal M_i}(1)
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
 \left[\frac12+t_i\left\{\mathbf 1(u=a)-\frac34\right\}\right]P(U=u)\\
 &=\frac12+t_i\left(\frac12-\frac34\right)\\
 &=\frac12-\frac{t_i}{4}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
It follows that
\[
 Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(1)=\frac7{16},
 \qquad
 Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(1)=\frac9{16}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}observational\text{-}fiber}\), both models lie in \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), but their interventional laws differ. Thus the displayed colored hedge has two strictly positive observationally equivalent witnesses with different \(Q_a\).

It remains to prove that no universal binary witness can match this observed law and to establish the general support claim. Let \(W\) be always observed and define
\[
 S_W=\{w:P_{\mathrm{obs}}(W=w)>0\}.
\]
In any model inducing \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), the observed value of \(W\) is its substantive value, so
\[
 S_W\subseteq\mathcal X_W
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 |\mathcal X_W|\geq |S_W|.
\]
For a partially observed substantive coordinate \(W\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}proxy\text{-}consistency}\) gives \(W^{\dagger}=W\) on \(R_W=1\). The required conditioning event has positive probability under \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}positivity}\): by \(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\text{-}alphabets}\), summing the finitely many positive full-data cells with \(R_W=1\) gives \(P_{\mathcal M}(R_W=1)>0\). Consequently
\[
 S_W^{\dagger}
 =\operatorname{supp}_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}(W^{\dagger}\mid R_W=1)
 \subseteq\mathcal X_W,
\]
and hence
\[
 |\mathcal X_W|\geq |S_W^{\dagger}|.
\]

Under \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}positivity}\), both inclusions are equalities at the level of supports. Indeed, for every \(w\in\mathcal X_W\), summing the positive full-data cells whose substantive coordinate is \(W=w\) yields
\[
 P_{\mathcal M}(W=w)>0
\]
when \(W\) is always observed. If \(W\) is partially observed, summing the positive full-data cells with \(W=w\) and \(R_W=1\) gives
\[
 P_{\mathcal M}(W=w,R_W=1)>0.
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass{:}proxy\text{-}consistency}\), this equals
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}(W^{\dagger}=w,R_W=1)>0.
\]
Thus every declared substantive value occurs in the conditional proxy support. Conversely, proxy consistency permits no value outside \(\mathcal X_W\) on \(R_W=1\). We have therefore proved
\[
 |S_W|=|\mathcal X_W|
 \quad\text{for always-observed }W,
 \qquad
 |S_W^{\dagger}|=|\mathcal X_W|
 \quad\text{for partially observed }W.
\]

In the constructed common law, \(S_Z=\{0,1,2\}\). Hence every model matching \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) must satisfy \(|\mathcal X_Z|\geq3\), so no such model can make every substantive variable binary. This disproves the universal binary-witness assertion.

Finally, for an arbitrary integer \(m\geq2\), replace \(\mathcal X_Z\) by \(\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\) and take \(E_Z\) uniform on it, leaving the equations for \(A\) and \(Y\) unchanged. The same computation gives two strictly positive models with a common observed law and distinct query values. The forests \(\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F\), their districts and roots, the empty coloring, and the trace family are unchanged because \(Z\) is isolated and belongs to neither forest. On the other hand, the observed support of \(Z\) has cardinality \(m\), so the support argument forces \(|\mathcal X_Z|\geq m\); the displayed construction attains equality. Thus the smallest required \(Z\)-alphabet coordinate is \(m\), while the colored hedge data are fixed. Since \(m\) is arbitrary, the smallest substantive alphabet vector is not determined by the color and district structure of a colored hedge alone. This proves every assertion of the theorem.

prose_overlay.tldr: Finite labeled-missingness graphs encode context-specific mechanism deletions, but restricting to a missingness context too early can discard an identifying pre-restriction kernel. The procedure \(\operatorname{TCF}(\mathcal G,A,Y,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) first constructs finite semialgebraic coordinate and direct score-contrast partitions from an edge-factorized response-function presentation, and then annotates fixed cells only with trace expressions verified on the whole cell. A coordinate or the declared score-coded NATE is recovered exactly when it is constant on the finite positive observational fiber; otherwise the corresponding negative cell yields two strictly positive same-observed lm-SCMs with different query values. Exact input is needed only to represent such witnesses, after which a finite diagnostic returns either a checked first-divergence record or an exhaustion tag, not a colored hedge. Figure 3(b) supplies the fix-then-select witness. On the common finite positive class, TCF preserves the de Aguas Proposition 4 and Mokhtarian root-control functionals, strictly extends the former on the endogenous-indicator proxy front-door family, and treats the latter as an embedding whose root premise is inapplicable to that family.
prose_overlay.related_work: De Aguas et al. (2025), Proposition 4 and Figure 3(b), are the first direct comparator: the proposition gives a weighted context-adjustment functional, and the figure exhibits fix-before-select information flow. Mokhtarian et al. (2022), Theorem 1, Corollary 2, and Algorithm 1, provide the second theorem-level comparator: their context-by-context algorithm is complete when context variables are observed causal roots. Theorem \(\text{thm:two-comparator-strict-extension}\) preserves both functionals on the common finite positive subclass, proves strict extension only of the de Aguas Proposition 4 criterion on \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{EIPFD}}\), and records that the root-control premise fails there without claiming strictness over the complete root-control domain. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (2019) inform sound finite CSI search, and Bhattacharya et al. (2020) inform recursive removal in missing-data graphs, but neither carries the label-license provenance used here. Richardson et al. (2023) prove ordinary fixing-order invariance; the colored adjacent-swap result preserves the uncolored kernel while retaining order-sensitive provenance and never commutes fixing with selection. Shpitser and Pearl (2006) supply the ordinary ID and hedge background, but this note does not prove a colored-hedge converse. Duarte et al. (2023) motivate response-function polynomialization; the present response-fiber theorem adds the lm-specific individual-edge product structure and strict full-data positivity needed for the exact pointwise dichotomy.
prose_overlay.interpretation: The observable decision and the causal target remain distinct. On a positive target cell, the unique semialgebraic value or a verified rational trace is proved equal to \(\tau_{s_Y}^{\mathcal M}\) for every model in the observed-law fiber. On a negative target cell, two models have the same proxy law but unequal score contrasts, so no observed-law functional can identify that target on the class. For the ADHD medication and test-achievement consumer, the method can test outcome-distribution FATE coordinates and the score-coded NATE separately; the Figure 3(b) calculation explains why the medication kernel must sometimes be fixed before conditioning on a missing pre-test indicator.
prose_overlay.technical_internal_limitation: Completeness is pointwise and semialgebraic on the finite strictly positive regular-maximal subclass. The diagnostic compiler tests candidate first-divergence records but neither tag certifies a colored hedge, realizes a rooted forest, or aligns an algebraic witness with a failed graphical recursion; graphwise colored-hedge completeness therefore remains unproved. Negative finite-subclass witnesses transfer to the larger published ambient class, but positive identification on the finite subclass does not establish ambient identification for continuous or nonpositive models. The explicit CAD and trace bounds prove termination only and may be very large. The adjacent-swap lemma is local, and Figure 3(b) precludes treating fixing and context selection as generally commuting operations.
prose_overlay.honest_scope: The graph, labels, finite alphabets, treatment, outcome, treatment endpoints, and real outcome score are supplied. Theorems range over nonempty observational fibers of finite-state, semi-Markovian, strictly full-data-positive, regular-maximal labeled-missingness SCMs. TCF gives a finite symbolic partition and a complete iff constancy decision for each interventional coordinate and for the declared score contrast; negative cells yield strictly positive individual-edge-factorized same-observed countermodels without any exact representation assumption. Exact observed and score interfaces are required only for algorithmic cell selection, represented value or witness extraction, and the optional finite divergence diagnostic. The procedure returns no colored hedge and makes no graphwise colored-hedge completeness claim. Negative finite witnesses imply nonidentification in the larger published ambient class, while positive finite-subclass results are not asserted for continuous, nonpositive, or merely observed-positive models. Estimation, graph learning, and finite-sample inference are outside scope, and no polynomial-time claim is made.

project_justification.gap: De Aguas et al. give a sufficient weighted-adjustment criterion and the Figure 3(b) fix-before-select recovery, while Mokhtarian et al. give completeness when observed context variables are causal roots. Neither result supplies a single finite procedure that preserves pre-restriction proxy traces, tests both interventional coordinates and a score contrast directly, and returns positive same-observed countermodels whenever the relevant finite response fiber is nonconstant.
project_justification.niche: For finite strictly positive regular-maximal lm-graphs, individual-edge semi-Markovian response functions turn the observational fiber and intervention queries into a finite polynomial system. Trace-aware colored fixing can then be used as an expression-discovery layer while semialgebraic constancy, rather than a graphwise failure converse, supplies the complete pointwise decision.
project_justification.fill: The note gives a two-way response-fiber equivalence, separate finite semialgebraic partitions for every interventional coordinate and for the declared score contrast, whole-cell verification of trace expressions, exact-free positive countermodel existence on negative cells, an exact-input representation and finite diagnostic compiler, and an explicit terminating CAD budget. It also proves the Figure 3(b) operation-order witness, preserves both published comparator functionals on their common finite positive domain, and establishes strict extension of the de Aguas Proposition 4 criterion through the delayed-selection front-door functional on \(\mathcal G_\star\) and its EIPFD family.

sampling_model.design: Population exact recovery from a supplied finite regular-maximal labeled-missingness graph. The mathematical output is a coordinate partition over feasible observed-cell laws and a direct target partition over observed-cell and real score coordinates; graph learning and finite-sample inference are outside the core.
sampling_model.overlap: Every full-data cell is strictly positive in the TCF subclass, making selected cells and every validated fixing denominator nonzero. This support restriction is not part of the supplied ambient-class definition.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no nuisance estimation in the exact-identification core. Mathematical constancy and exact-free countermodel existence hold for arbitrary compatible population coordinates and real scores; represented cell selection or witness extraction additionally requires rational or real-algebraic coordinates with isolating data, or an exact-real polynomial-sign oracle.
sampling_model.units: Independent draws of the observed record \(\mathcal O\) are the eventual statistical input, while the identification theorem treats all observed-cell probabilities as formal population coordinates.
sampling_model.treatment: The supplied treatment endpoints \(a_0,a_1\in\mathcal X_A\) define the natural intervention contrast. Coordinate-level FATE queries \(Q_a(y)\) and the score-coded NATE \(\tau_{s_Y}\) are tested separately.

thm:tcf-termination.justification: The finite guarantee counts complete trace histories, both trace-independent CAD partitions, and every coordinate or target annotation validation.
thm:tcf-termination.gap: The direct score branch adds formal score dimensions and a second base elimination that must be charged explicitly.
thm:tcf-termination.consumer: Small-graph exact audits can enumerate all traces and compare both the coordinate and target cells with response-function elimination.

thm:qe-failure-compiler.justification: An exact negative cell yields a directly checkable positive lm-SCM pair, while the optional scan honestly reports either a verified candidate record or exhaustion.
thm:qe-failure-compiler.gap: No graph-only induction invariant presently forces colored-hedge existence or aligns the algebraic pair with a recursion failure.
thm:qe-failure-compiler.consumer: Investigators can audit the response tables, individual latent factors, observed-law equality, and differing causal coordinate.

thm:colored-completeness.justification: The flagship theorem is now iff for the declared score contrast itself while retaining all coordinatewise recovery and countermodel conclusions.
thm:colored-completeness.gap: The theorem does not transfer positive identification to the ambient class and does not turn algebraic nonconstancy into a graphwise colored hedge.
thm:colored-completeness.consumer: ADHD medication and test achievement receive separate exact FATE-coordinate and NATE decisions, including cases where only the contrast is constant.

thm:response-fiber-equivalence.justification: The theorem proves equality with the finite TCF fiber while preserving each individual bidirected-edge factor; it does not identify that subclass with the published ambient model.
thm:response-fiber-equivalence.gap: Generic response-function polynomialization does not supply the universal factor support, exact label deletions, or the two-way finite lm-fiber decoding.
thm:response-fiber-equivalence.consumer: Every positive or negative cell can be interpreted as a statement about actual finite full-positive lm-SCMs, and negative pairs can then be transferred to the ambient class.

lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy.justification: The lemma separates coordinate constancy from direct score-contrast constancy and gives a computable semialgebraic side for each.
lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy.gap: Coordinatewise identification is sufficient but not necessary for target identification because nonconstant coordinates can cancel under the supplied score.
lem:semialgebraic-fiber-dichotomy.consumer: The ADHD analysis can decide FATE coordinates and NATE directly rather than treating a failed coordinate as a failed scalar target.

thm:two-comparator-strict-extension.justification: The theorem makes the comparison at the domain actually proved: a strict de Aguas criterion extension and a Mokhtarian root-control embedding on the common finite positive intersection.
thm:two-comparator-strict-extension.gap: No theorem here extends EIPFD identification to the categorical-or-continuous ambient class under only observed-data positivity.
thm:two-comparator-strict-extension.consumer: Applied users retain the published formula when its source conditions hold on the common subclass and obtain the delayed-selection front-door formula for the finite positive EIPFD family.

prop:ambient-nonrecovery-transfer.justification: Either a coordinate-level or target-level finite positive countermodel pair is already a countermodel pair in the larger published ambient class.
prop:ambient-nonrecovery-transfer.gap: Exact witness representation is algorithmic extra structure and is not a premise of existential ambient nonidentification.
prop:ambient-nonrecovery-transfer.consumer: A negative direct NATE cell certifies ambient failure even when no exact numerical extraction oracle is supplied.
